1.title: Usability and Storytelling: Bookmarks, Tooltips, Navigation, Drillthrough
1.text: Welcome to Module eleven: Usability and Storytelling: Bookmarks, Tooltips, Navigation, Drillthrough. It covers the exam area Visualize and analyze the data. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do seven things. Configure bookmarks. Create custom tooltips. Edit and configure interactions between visuals. Configure navigation for a report. Apply sorting to visuals. Configure sync slicers. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Visualize and analyze the data (twenty-five-thirty percent). Exam format: a one hundred-minute proctored exam; a score of seven hundred on a scale to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official P L three hundred study guide, skills measured as of April twenty, twenty twenty-six.

1.title: Drillthrough and its look-alikes
1.text: Drillthrough and its look-alikes. Drillthrough sends the viewer from a summary to a detail page that is already filtered to the item they picked.

1.title: Drillthrough and its look-alikes, continued
1.text: Drillthrough and its look-alikes. The figure shows this: Drillthrough: a viewer right-clicks a data point on a summary page and lands on a detail page filtered to that item, with an automatic Back button.

1.title: Drillthrough and its look-alikes, continued
1.text: Drillthrough and its look-alikes. Drill down. Moves down a hierarchy inside the same visual, such as Year, Quarter, Month. Drill through. Jumps to another page, filtered by the selected item. Cross-filtering. Selecting a data point filters or highlights the other visuals on the same page.

1.title: Drillthrough and its look-alikes, continued
1.text: Drillthrough and its look-alikes. one. Create the page. Add a detail page and give it a clear name. two. Add the field. Drag the field into the Drillthrough filters well; Power B I adds a Back button automatically. three. Use it. Viewers right-click a data point, choose Drillthrough, then the page. four. Or use a button. Add a button whose Action type is Drill through.

1.title: Drillthrough and its look-alikes, continued
1.text: Drillthrough and its look-alikes. The well also offers a Keep all filters switch, which passes the other filters of the source page along. Cross-report drillthrough works when both reports are in the same workspace, the target report has Cross-report drillthrough turned on, and the field names and types match. Exam tip: Drill down stays in the visual, drill through goes to another page, cross-filtering stays on the page. If a scenario says "open a detail page for the selected item", the answer is drillthrough.

1.title: Bookmarks
1.text: Bookmarks. A bookmark saves the state of a report page so that one click returns to it. It captures the current page, filters, slicers, visual selection, sort, drill location, visibility of objects and focus mode. Open the Bookmarks pane on the View tab.

1.title: Bookmarks, continued
1.text: Bookmarks. Data. Filters, slicers, sort and drill location. Display. Which objects are shown or hidden, and focus mode. Current page. The page that is showing; turned off, the viewer stays on the current page. All visuals or Selected visuals. Whether the bookmark affects every visual or only the selected ones. Related features. Groups keep related bookmarks together in the pane. Slideshow: the View button in the Bookmarks pane steps through the bookmarks in order. Button action Bookmark: a button runs a chosen bookmark. Bookmark navigator: one button for every bookmark, added from Insert, Buttons, Navigator.

1.title: Bookmarks, continued
1.text: Bookmarks. A slicer added after a bookmark was saved is cleared when that bookmark is applied. Exam tip: A bookmark restores a saved view of the same report; drillthrough opens a page filtered by the chosen item. Data, Display and Current page can each be switched off for a bookmark.

1.title: Navigation, buttons and tooltips
1.text: Navigation, buttons and tooltips. Navigation is built from navigators and buttons. Add them from the Insert tab, Buttons. Page navigator. One button for every page, built automatically. Bookmark navigator. One button for every bookmark. Button. A shape with one action.

1.title: Navigation, buttons and tooltips, continued
1.text: Navigation, buttons and tooltips. A button action can be Back, Bookmark, Drill through, Page navigation, Q and A, Web U R L, Apply all slicers or Clear all slicers. The destination of a page navigation button can be conditional, driven by a field with fx. A custom tooltip is a small report page that appears when the viewer hovers over a visual.

1.title: Navigation, buttons and tooltips, continued
1.text: Navigation, buttons and tooltips. one. Page size. In Format page, set the page size to Tooltip. two. Page information. Turn on Allow use as tooltip. three. Tooltip fields well. Add the field that the tooltip page should filter by. four. Visuals. Build small visuals on the page. five. Set it on a visual. Format visual, Tooltips, Type Report page, then choose the page. Tooltips are not interactive: the viewer can hover, not click. Exam tip: A tooltip page needs page size Tooltip and Allow use as tooltip turned on; then each visual must use Type Report page. Skipping the last step leaves the default tooltip.

1.title: Interactions, sorting and sync slicers
1.text: Interactions, sorting and sync slicers. Interactions decide what happens to other visuals when you select a data point. Select the source visual, choose Edit interactions on the Format tab, then click an icon on each target visual. Filter. Shows only the selected data. Highlight. Shows all data with the selected part highlighted. None. No effect. The default is cross-filtering or cross-highlighting. Line charts, scatter charts and maps are filtered, not highlighted. Drilling down in one visual filters the others only when Apply drill down filters to is set to Entire page.

1.title: Interactions, sorting and sync slicers, continued
1.text: Interactions, sorting and sync slicers. Sorting. On a visual, open More options, choose Sort axis, pick a field and sort ascending or descending. In the model, Sort by column fixes a text column that sorts alphabetically: sort Month Name by Month Number. Each name must map to one number. Sync slicers. Open the Sync slicers pane on the View tab.

1.title: Interactions, sorting and sync slicers, continued
1.text: Interactions, sorting and sync slicers. Sync. The slicer's selections apply on that page. Visible. The slicer is shown on that page. A synced slicer that is not visible still filters its page. In Advanced options, a group name syncs separate slicers that share the name, with options to sync field changes and filter changes. Exam tip: Sync controls where the selection applies; Visible controls where the slicer appears. Sync on with Visible off filters a page silently.

2.title: The Selection pane
2.text: The Selection pane. The Selection pane lists every object on the page. Open it on the View tab. Layer order. Objects higher in the list are in front; drag to reorder. Show or hide. The eye icon hides an object without deleting it. Group. Group several objects to move, resize or hide them together. Rename. Give clear names to find objects quickly. Tab order. Sets the keyboard order; remove decorative items. Bookmarks save the eye icon state through the Display option, which makes view switching possible. Exam tip: The top of the Selection pane list is the front layer, and bookmarks save which objects are hidden. Grouping does not change interactions.

2.title: Practice Question 1
2.text: Question one. Users on a summary page want to right-click a customer and open a detail page that shows only that customer. What should the author do on the detail page? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Add the Customer field to the Drillthrough filters well. A field in the Drillthrough filters well makes the page a drillthrough target that is filtered to the item chosen on the source page.

2.title: Practice Question 2
2.text: Question two. An author wants buttons that switch one page between a chart view and a table view by showing and hiding visuals. What should the author combine? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Two bookmarks that save visibility, and buttons that run them. Bookmarks capture the Display state set in the Selection pane, and buttons with the Bookmark action run them.

2.title: Practice Question 3
2.text: Question three. An author set a page to the Tooltip size and turned on Allow use as tooltip, but hovering over the visual still shows the default tooltip. What step is missing? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Set the tooltip Type to Report page on the visual. Each visual must be pointed at the tooltip page with Type Report page, otherwise it keeps the default tooltip.

2.title: Practice Question 4
2.text: Question four. A Year slicer on page one must filter pages two and three, and no slicer should appear on those pages. How should the author set pages two and three in the Sync slicers pane? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Sync on and Visible off for pages two and three. Sync applies the selection on the page and Visible off hides the slicer, and a synced slicer that is hidden still filters.

2.title: Practice Question 5
2.text: Question five. Selecting a bar in a column chart should filter a matrix on the same page but leave a card unchanged. What should the author do? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Use Edit interactions on the chart and set the card to None. Edit interactions with None on the card stops the chart from affecting it, while grouping, layers and sync do not control interactions.

2.title: Practice Question 6
2.text: Question six. A column chart lists months as April, August, December and so on. The author wants calendar order. What should the author do? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Set Month Name to sort by Month Number in the model. Sort by column in the model sorts the month names by their month numbers in every visual.

2.title: Recall Check 1
2.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Which three options can a bookmark include or leave out? Answer: Data, Display and Current page. Question two. What are the three interaction icons? Answer: Filter, Highlight and None. Question three. Which page size and Page information switch make a tooltip page? Answer: Tooltip size, and Allow use as tooltip.

2.title: Recall Check 2
2.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What does the Visible column in Sync slicers do? Answer: It shows the slicer on that page. Question five. Which end of the Selection pane list is the front layer? Answer: The top. Question six. Which feature jumps to another page filtered by the selected item? Answer: Drillthrough.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. Drill features: Drill down: inside the visual; drill through: another page; cross-filtering: same page. Drillthrough: Field in the Drillthrough filters well; automatic Back button; right-click or button. Bookmarks: Page, filters, slicers, sort, drill, visibility; options Data, Display, Current page; groups, slideshow. Navigation: Page navigator, bookmark navigator, buttons with actions such as Back, Bookmark, Drill through. Tooltips: Page size Tooltip; Allow use as tooltip; Type Report page; not interactive. Interactions: Filter, Highlight, None; line charts, scatter charts and maps only filter. Sorting: Sort axis on the visual; Sort by column in the model for month names. Sync slicers: Sync applies the selection; Visible shows the slicer; hidden synced slicers still filter.
